source.title: Embedding Principle of Loss Landscape of Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Yaoyu Zhang; Zhongwang Zhang; Tao Luo; Z. Xu

record.tranche_reason: The paper develops and illustrates an embedding principle for critical points in fully connected networks. Its experiments do not test the listed claims about natural-label test error, generalization gaps, or measures that track those gaps.
record.gate_note: The MNIST experiment reports prediction agreement between an original network and a reduced network on test data. This is not a test of test error or the train–test gap, so it is recorded under fits_no_version rather than mapped to a claim version.
record.test_reason: The study proves properties of critical-point embeddings and illustrates network reduction. It reports no comparison of held-out errors or generalization gaps that tests V1–V8. Its MNIST prediction agreement measures similarity between networks, not accuracy against true labels.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors prove that critical points of narrower fully connected networks can be embedded into wider networks while preserving output functions and increasing degeneracy under stated conditions. Their experiments suggest that training can approach such low-complexity critical points, providing a potential implicit regularization mechanism; they do not establish improved generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments study critical points and prediction similarity under specified training setups; they do not reproduce the original methods in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The text states that similar phenomena can be observed with properly small initialization variance; the MNIST prediction comparison is a case study based on one random trial.

fits_no_version.finding: The width-400 MNIST network and its reduced, subsequently trained width-58 counterpart agree on approximately 98.5% of predictions across 10000 test examples at the selected stagnation points.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A wide network near a critical point can admit a substantially narrower network with similar predictions.

record.problems: The MNIST result is a case study based on a random trial. The text reports prediction agreement, not test accuracy or a generalization gap.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization, including chance-level held-out accuracy with random labels.
Test-error changes when widening beyond the width required for zero training error.
Image test-error comparisons between convolutional and fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Held-out performance comparisons between adaptive optimizers and SGD under different tuning regimes.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce those effects.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness correlations with generalization gaps and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples compared with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: Hessian degeneracy and the illustrative synthetic fits do not test magnitude-aware sharpness or any other listed version. Figures 1 and 5 are single-trial case studies.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not compare natural labels with random labels or report held-out accuracy relative to chance.
The paper does not sweep network width to measure test error beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
The paper does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks on image test error.
The paper does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out performance.
The paper does not compare batch sizes or measure a large-batch generalization gap.
The paper does not test dropout or its effect on held-out error.
The paper does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with train–test gaps.
The paper does not remove memorized examples and measure the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: width-400 two-layer ReLU NN
rows.operation_detail: Compared predictions with those of a reduced width-58 network at the selected training point.
rows.measure: Prediction agreement between original and reduced networks
rows.note: The reported agreement compares two networks' predictions; it does not report test accuracy or a train–test gap.
rows.check: The approximately 98.5% agreement is correctly reported. Clarify that the reduced width-58 network was trained after reduction until it stagnated at approximately the original network's selected loss; predictions are compared at the respective blue points in Fig. 5(a,c). Agreement cannot establish either network's test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
